subject: Morpheus: p95 floor exemption request and cross-functional asks
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@morpheus.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@morpheus.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: p95 target for production deployment

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re prepping to go live with Morpheus Search (beta) the week of July 9 and have one ask that’s come up from our SRE and product teams: we need a contractual uptime + latency commitment for the critical search API routes. Specifically:

- p95 end-to-end latency <= 45ms for the /search and /rerank endpoints (US customers only)
- Sustained traffic: 9k RPS peak; steady-state 2k RPS
- 5% burst allowance up to 20k RPS for short windows (<= 5m)

Can Redwood approve an SLA carveout for this strategic deployment? We’ve attached our internal requirements (morpheus_sla_requirements.pdf).

If this needs a cross-functional alignment/exception, please route to product & infra. We’re happy to join a call to walk the traffic profile and priorities.

Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform, Morpheus AI
elena.torres@morpheus.ai

Attachment: morpheus_sla_requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: p95 target for production deployment — need product/infra + commercial tradeoffs

Team — forwarding a direct ask from Morpheus (DEAL-10243). They want a p95 <= 45ms for two critical routes in US with high sustained RPS and burst allowance. This would be a bespoke SLA carveout for a strategic account; they’re willing to sign a contract if we can commit.

Quick asks from me:
- Product/Infra (Karthik, Monica): feasibility and what changes (dedicated pool, kernel changes, cache warmups) are required. Rough timeline and risk to broader fleet.
- Sales/Finance (Marissa, Aditya): commercial offset (credits/commitment) we need to surface to legal & procurement.
- Legal: we’ll need an SLA addendum with clear failure modes and limited scope (US only, specific endpoints).

What I’d like to see in the first response today: top-level feasibility (yes/no), two alternative commitments we could make (e.g., dedicated capacity -> 45ms p95 vs. staged rollout -> 60ms p95 w/ prioritization), and the minimum commercial ask to cover infra changes.

I’m looping you all because this will require feature/ops work and a short-term carveout. If we can’t hit 45ms broadly, propose a hybrid: 45ms for 90% of traffic + fallback to a slightly higher-latency variant for the remainder.

— Vivek

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: p95 target for production deployment — product feasibility notes

Folks — quick feasibility note after an initial pass:

Short answer: technically achievable with conditions.

Constraints & requirements:
- 45ms end-to-end p95 is aggressive for general-purpose inference across mixed models. We can hit it for targeted endpoints if we:
  - Provision a dedicated GPU pool (low multitenancy noise)
  - Serve a quantized model variant optimized for latency on the target routes
  - Implement aggressive KV cache pre-warming and prefix caching for common queries
  - Ensure network path (US-west region) has priority routing and reduced hops

Trade-offs and alternatives:
- Option A (full carveout): Dedicated capacity + optimized model variant -> target 45ms p95 after tuning. Estimated infra delta: +2x baseline for those endpoints. Timeline: 3–4 weeks (dev + validation + 1-week soak).
- Option B (staged): Canary 60ms p95 for 100% traffic, then optimize to 45ms for 90% of traffic with fallback variant for edge cases. Lower infra cost, timeline 2–3 weeks.

Telemetry & runbook needs (required for SLA enforcement):
- Detailed SLI/SLO definitions per endpoint (p50/p95/p99, error rates, tail latency)
- KV cache hit rates and cold-start detection telemetry
- Automated routing fallback on SLA breach (shift traffic to alternative model variant)

I’ll put a short mitigation proposal together (latency-mitigation-proposal.md) and coordinate with Ops for load test plan. Need approval to reserve a dedicated pool and temporary override for autoscaling policies during the initial rollout.

— Karthik
Product — Serving & Inference

Attachment: latency-mitigation-proposal.md (md)

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: p95 target for production deployment — ops/runbook and risk

Adding Ops perspective:

Operational requirements to support Option A (dedicated pool):
- Dedicated GPU pool in us-west (estimate: 12 GPUs initially; will refine after load test)
- Canary plan: 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% over a 1 week period with a 72h soak at each step
- Load test: two simulated patterns (steady 2k RPS and peak 9k RPS with 5% bursts).
- Runbook for SLA alarms & automated rollback. We’ll need:
  1) Playbook to throttle non-critical routes if we see degradation
  2) Automated KV cache priming job ahead of deploy windows
  3) Visibility: token-level cost + per-route latency breakdown in Console

Risks:
- Isolation: without strict isolation, other high-load customers may cause p95 variance.
- Cost: dedicated pool increases unit cost; recommend a one-time infra credit in the commercial offer.

I’m attaching a draft runbook and a load test plan. If Sales wants to move forward we need sign-off on the dedicated pool allocation and an agreed credit to offset the first 6–8 weeks of infra spend.

— Monica
Operations/Production

Attachments: runbook_playbook.md (md), load_test_plan.jmx (jmx)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: p95 target for production deployment — commercial proposal

Commercial proposal to present to Morpheus:
- Offer: 25% committed usage discount (12-month commit) + one-time infrastructure onboarding credit of $50,000 to cover dedicated pool ramp-up costs.
- SLA scope: US-only routes (/search, /rerank), explicit carveout in SLA addendum, defined SLI/SLOs, and 30-day rollback clause if production impact observed.
- Billing & procurement: require a signed addendum and a 30-day notice for any capacity downgrades. Procurement will request contract language; route to Legal for redlines.

I’ve created a HubSpot deal link (see related_links) and will draft the commercial term sheet once Product/Ops confirm timeline and GPU count.

— Aditya
Sales Ops / Finance

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Morpheus p95 carveout — conditional approval

All — thanks for the fast turnaround. I’m OK approving the carveout for Morpheus on the following conditions:

1) Product & Ops deliver a concrete timeline (firm dates) for the 3–4 week Option A plan and provide the load test results before any full traffic cutover.
2) Finance provides the commercial term sheet with the $50k onboarding credit and the 12-month commitment discount.
3) Legal drafts an SLA addendum limiting scope to the specified endpoints/region with clear M&Ps and rollback language.

Next steps: Vivek, please schedule a 30-minute alignment call with Morpheus + Product + Ops + Sales + Legal tomorrow EOD. Karthik/Monica, have the runbook and load test plan ready for that call; Aditya, get the term sheet draft into the drive link.

If we hit the checkpoints above, we’ll sign the addendum and allocate the dedicated pool. Keep the execs updated if any of the timelines slide.

— Marissa
VP Sales
Redwood Inference
